items.quote: Glasgow is the most populous city in Scotland, located on the banks of the River Clyde
The Old Firm is a collective term for the Scottish football clubs Celtic and Rangers
nickname, "The Clockwork Orange" (coined from the title of the book and film A Clockwork Orange) is subject to dispute
items.note: Answer is sound, but the premise "because of the colour of its trains" is shakier than it reads: Wikipedia says the nickname is seldom used outside the press and was coined from the book/film title, with its origin disputed. Safer wording: "Glasgow's Subway, with its orange carriages, is nicknamed the 'Clockwork' what?"

items.quote: Since at least the 1980s it has been traditionally capped with a traffic cone by members of the public
The most famous of its buildings was designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh and Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh
items.note: Wikipedia now co-credits Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh, but she was not Glasgow-born, so "Glasgow-born architect" still yields one answer. The Mackintosh Building was gutted by fires in 2014 and 2018; "best-known building" still holds.

items.quote: This was abbreviated to "Let Glasgow Flourish" and adopted as the city's motto
known as Mungo, was a missionary in the Brittonic Kingdom of Strathclyde in the late sixth century, and the founder and patron saint of the city of Glasgow
items.note: The question gives "Kentigern", which is the same saint, so a room that knows one name knows the other; fine as a gimme.

items.quote: Three fish are depicted in the coat of arms, each with a ring in its mouth
items.note: The rhyme itself sits in a template the checker strips, so the quote is the coat-of-arms description instead. Accept "salmon".

items.quote: is in the collection of the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow
The SEC Armadillo (originally known as the Clyde Auditorium) is an auditorium located near the River Clyde
items.note: Out of date framing: the venue's official name is now the SEC Armadillo; "Clyde Auditorium" is its original name, so "better known by the nickname" is no longer true, and the question half-gives the answer away. Reword: "Glasgow's riverside concert venue, originally called the Clyde Auditorium, is now officially named after which armoured animal?"
